blocks.content: The geographic grid forms an essential network of intersecting latitudes and longitudes that enables exact location pin-pointing and global time determination.

Determining local time and time zones

items: Tropic of Cancer (23°30' N) passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.
Indian Standard Time (82°30' E) passes through 5 states: Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh.
Crossing the International Date Line (180° Meridian) from West to East gains a day, while crossing East to West loses a day.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The geographic grid is a network of intersecting parallels of latitude and meridians of longitude used to pinpoint exact locations on Earth.
Latitudes are parallel horizontal lines ranging from 0° at the Equator to 90° North and South at the Poles.
Longitudes are vertical semi-circles running from Pole to Pole, with 0° anchored at the Prime Meridian in Greenwich, London.
Because Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours, every 15° of longitude equals 1 hour of time difference, or 4 minutes per 1°.
Indian Standard Time (IST) is calculated from 82°30' E longitude, putting India 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of GMT.
